from.place: proof, finite-algebra calculation: spread the purely inseparable residual field factors and localize so that they are finite radicial covers

title: Spreading purely inseparable factors
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian integral domain with fraction field $K$, let $A'$ be a finite etale $A$-algebra [def-weil-etale-morphism] that is a domain with fraction field $K'$, and let $E$ be a finite $A'$-algebra that is a domain with fraction field $L$, where $L/K'$ is finite purely inseparable [def-pc-field-extension] [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. There is a nonzero $s\in A$ such that, with $A_1=A[1/s]$, $A'_1=A'\otimes_AA_1$, and $E_1=E\otimes_AA_1$, the induced morphism $\operatorname{Spec}(E_1)\to\operatorname{Spec}(A'_1)$ is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism] and radicial [def-weil-radicial-morphism], hence a universal homeomorphism [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism].

source.place: proof, finite-algebra calculation, purely inseparable factors and universal-homeomorphism conclusion (Stacks Tags 00GQ, 0BR5, 01S2)

proof.text: Because E is finite over A', it is integral over A'. The inclusion A' to E is injective because it induces the stated inclusion of fraction fields. After the indicated principal localization, lying over gives a prime of E_1 above every prime of A'_1, so Spec(E_1) to Spec(A'_1) is surjective.

source.place: Lemma 00GQ (lying over), applied to the finite algebra

proof.text: A' is finite over the Noetherian domain A, hence Noetherian, so the power-in-base node applies to E over A' and gives a nonzero s' in A'. Since A' is a domain integral over A, take a monic equation s'^m+a_{m-1}s'^{m-1}+...+a_0=0 over A of minimal degree; then a_0 is nonzero and a_0 = s'*(element of A'), so s=a_0 in A is nonzero and A'[1/s] is a localization of A'[1/s'], E_1=E[1/s]; the power property persists under this further localization. In characteristic zero E_1=A'_1, so the morphism is an isomorphism. In characteristic p>0 every x in E_1 has x^{p^n} in the image of A'_1. Hence two primes q, q' of E_1 over the same prime P of A'_1 coincide (x in q iff x^{p^n} in P iff x in q'), so Spec(E_1) to Spec(A'_1) is injective; and every element of a residue field of E_1, being a quotient of images of elements of E_1, has a p^n-th power in the residue field of A'_1, so each residue-field extension is purely inseparable. By the radicial definition (Stacks 01S4) the morphism is radicial, equivalently universally injective.

source.place: Lemma 01S4 (radicial iff universally injective, via purely inseparable residue fields)

proof.text: The preceding steps give an integral, surjective and radicial morphism. Applying the integral-radicial-surjective universal-homeomorphism criterion yields that Spec(E_1) to Spec(A'_1) is a universal homeomorphism.
